option.approach: Determine whether the faithful normalized 2-quasitrace supplies an additional hypothesis absent from alleged counterexamples to sequential completeness. Compare those examples against every assumption in the problem before drawing a contradiction.

options.approach: Audit the exact hypotheses of the claimed sequential-completeness theorem. Identify whether its proof silently requires a linear trace, an additional continuity property, or a stronger completeness assumption.

options.counterfactual: A normalized 2-quasitrace need not tend to zero on the terms of a positive series whose finite partial sums are bounded by the identity.
options.approach: Examine whether such a positive series can exist specifically in a finite AW*-factor with a faithful quasitrace. Failure of exhaustivity in a broader class would not by itself produce an example for this problem.

options.counterfactual: A normalized 2-quasitrace need not tend to zero on the terms of a positive series whose finite partial sums are bounded by the identity.
options.approach: Starting with a nonexhaustive positive series, select terms with quasitrace bounded below and scale them individually to obtain equal quasitrace values. Then investigate the separate requirement that their increasing partial sums have no least upper bound.
